HomeStyle Retailers Inc. - Q2 FY2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the HomeStyle Retailers Inc. Q2 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please also note, today's event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and thank you for joining us today to discuss HomeStyle Retailers Inc.'s results for the Q2 FY2024. Joining me on today’s call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Patel, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Merchandising Officer; Tom Hargrove, Chief Stores Officer; and Emma Lopez, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

With that, I’ll turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I’m pleased to report HomeStyle Retailers Inc.'s performance for the Q2 FY2024. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities and delivered solid results despite the challenging macroeconomic environment.

Our results this quarter really highlight our resilience as a leading brick-and-mortar powerhouse with over 850 stores across North America, specializing in affordable home furnishings and décor. Net sales hit $2.85 billion, up 4.2% year-over-year, beating our guidance and consensus. This was our sixth straight quarter of positive comps at +2.8% on a 52-week basis, outpacing the broader specialty retail index. Traffic rose 1.2%, average unit retail increased 1.5% thanks to better mix and controlled promotions, and conversion stayed steady at 28.5%. Categories shone across the board: home essentials up 4.7% on kitchen and outdoor demand, apparel at +1.9%, and grocery consumables +2.1% with private-label strength. Gross margins expanded 140 basis points to 38.2% from cleaner inventories at 10.2 weeks and freight relief. SG&A improved 30 basis points to 25.1% through labor efficiencies, driving adjusted operating income to $285 million, up 12%, EBITDA to $410 million, and EPS to $1.28, up 16%. Regionally, Sunbelt markets led with +5.6% comps on population growth, while omnichannel now at 29% of sales accelerated +11%. These outcomes validate our brick-to-click fusion strategy, and we're raising full-year guidance across the board.

We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Patel to provide more details on our financial results.

Mike Patel, Chief Financial Officer:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning. I'll provide a more detailed review of our financial performance for the Q2 FY2024.

Our total revenue for the quarter was $2.85 billion, a 4.2% increase compared to the same period last year. Gross margin was 38.2%, primarily driven by supply chain efficiencies, reduced markdowns to 18.4% of sales, and favorable product mix with higher-margin hardlines. Operating expenses were $715 million, representing 25.1% of revenue, benefiting from AI-driven labor scheduling that cut overtime 22%. Net income was $285 million, or $1.28 per share. We generated $410 million in cash flow from operations. Inventory levels are currently at 10.2 weeks of supply, reflecting improved turns.

Before I go deeper, let me unpack our same-store sales—or comps—breakdown, focusing on traffic versus average ticket dynamics. As everyone knows, comps growth equals traffic growth times conversion times average ticket growth. We achieved a solid 4.2% comp increase, driven by +2.1% traffic, flat conversion at 98% of prior year levels, and +2.0% average ticket. Traffic led the way at +2.1% year-over-year, our sixth consecutive quarter of gains, beating specialty retail peers where Placer.ai shows just +0.8%. We hit 28.7 million store visits, up from 28.1 million last year. The 'Storefront Revival' initiative with experiential zones in 220 doors, including AR kitchen demos, lifted traffic 4.5% in those locations. BOPIS orders jumped 18%, increasing dwell time 12% via Wi-Fi data. Sunbelt regions—42% of stores in Florida, Texas, Carolinas—saw +4.2% from housing booms, while Northeast dipped -1.1% on weather and urban softness, and Midwest +1.3% from loyalty geo-fencing generating 1.2 million visits. We've upgraded to Sensormatic AI counters in 65% of doors for 95% accuracy, linking to gas prices and events like NFL games boosting weekends +7%.

On average ticket, up 2.0% to $128.45, with +1.8% ASP despite 3.2% COGS inflation, offset by dynamic pricing on textiles and value ladder upsells adding +0.2% units per transaction. West region tickets rose +3.1% to over $135 on premium collabs, Southeast +0.9%. Top doors averaged $152, 18% above chain. Conversion at 28.4% was flat, challenged by showrooming, but heatmaps and associate tech recovered 2.5%. Overall, this traffic-led profile shows omnichannel synergy, with digital driving 22% of store traffic. We're investing $150 million in more remodels for +3-5% traffic, loyalty at 14.2 million adding 50 basis points to ticket, and RFID pilots for conversion gains. Q3 comps guided +3.5-5.0%, traffic +2.5-3.5%.

Shifting to supply chain efficiencies, a major factor in our 220 basis point gross margin gain. OTIF hit 98.2%, up from 92.4%, cutting stockouts 18% and fueling comps. Turns rose to 7.2x from 6.1x, DIO to 48 days, freeing $185 million. Supply chain costs fell 14% to $420 million, inbound freight per unit down 22%. AI demand sensing cut forecast errors 28%, AMRs handle 65% picking for 35% throughput boost to 1.2 million cases daily. Nearshoring 42% sourcing to Mexico/Vietnam trimmed lead times to 22 days, UPS contracts saved 15%, truck utilization 92%. North America DCs gained 16% efficiency with micro-fulfillment for 96% same-day BOPIS. Europe pilots cut freight 19%, Asia RFID to 99.5% accuracy. This agility beats e-comm, benchmarking toward Walmart's turns, and cut Scope 3 emissions 12%. FY24 $250 million more for automation targets 10-12% further cuts.

Inventory turnover strengthened to 6.2x company-wide, up 15% from 5.4x, DIO 59 days versus 68, unlocking $250 million. Trailing 12-month at 6.5x tops Target's 5.8x. Apparel/softlines 4.8x from AI pricing reducing stockouts 22%, hardlines/home 7.1x via VMI with Whirlpool, electronics 9.4x on omnichannel. Southeast/Sunbelt 6.8x on traffic, Northeast/Midwest 5.4x countered by RFID, West 6.0x. Drivers: nearshoring to 45% Mexico/Vietnam, gen AI forecasting error to 8%, clustering analytics cut $80 million slow stock. Q4 turns 6.4-6.6x with holiday discipline.

Marketing and advertising expenses rose to $45.2 million, up 12% or 3.2% of sales from 2.8%. Full-year now 3.0-3.3%. Digital 62% at $28.1 million, up 22%, ROAS 5.2x on Google SEM for 'affordable home refresh', programmatic CAC down 15% to $28. Social $9.8 million drove 28% store traffic via Reels/TikTok, 4.5x ROAS for private label. Traditional $17.1 million flat, circulars 3.8x, pop-ups +18% traffic, loyalty app 14 million members drove 22% transactions. U.S. up 14% in Southeast recovery, international conservative in Europe, ramping in Asia. ML optimization improved efficiency 17%, blended ROAS 4.7x beats peers. Q4 adds retail media and sustainability stories.

For comp sales outlook, Q3 guide 3.5-5.5%, building on traffic +2.1%, EDLP, holiday omnichannel covering 95% SKUs. Essentials/private label up, AI pricing +150 bps, partnerships like Ulta/Starbucks +8-10%. Sunbelt 6-8%, Midwest 4-6%, Northeast 1-3%. FY2024 full 4-6%, with remodels +7.2% lift, retailtainment pilots, DC expansion cutting times 20%. Risks like Fed policy, but margins give power.

Broader outlook: Q3 net sales $4.85-4.95 billion, +2-4%, comps 1.5-3.5% with store 2-4%, e-comm flat-2%. Gross margin 38.2-38.7%, +50 bps from efficiencies, AI pricing, RFID shrink cuts. SG&A 27.5-28.0%, op income $550-600 million, EPS $0.85-0.95. Full FY2024 sales $15.6-15.8 billion, +3-5%, comps 2.5-4.0%, gross 38.0-38.5%, EPS $2.55-2.65, FCF >$1.2 billion. Sunbelt 5-7%, international +8%. FY25: 25 small-format stores, $650-700 million capex for remodels/micro-fulfillment, loyalty 28 million at 55% sales.

We are maintaining a strong balance sheet and are well positioned to invest in our growth initiatives.

Now, I'd like to hand it over to Lisa Chen, our Chief Merchandising Officer, to discuss our new product lines, followed by Tom Hargrove to discuss store operations, and then Emma Lopez to discuss marketing initiatives.

Lisa Chen, Chief Merchandising Officer:
Thank you, Mike. This quarter, we launched our Essentials Everyday private-label line expansion, which has seen exceptional sell-through exceeding plan by 12%, particularly in kitchen essentials and textiles. Comps in home goods jumped 4.7%, and we're excited about upcoming exclusives like Mohawk carpet collabs and seasonal patio sets, positioning us strongly for holiday.

Tom Hargrove, Chief Stores Officer:
Thank you, Lisa. We continue to focus on improving the customer experience in our stores. We have implemented Storefront Revival experiential zones and micro-fulfillment in high-density areas, delivering 4.5% traffic uplift and 96% same-day BOPIS, with positive results across our 850 doors, especially in Sunbelt remodels boosting dwell time 18%.

Emma Lopez, Chief Marketing Officer:
Thank you, Tom. Our Home Refresh campaign, leveraging digital SEM, social Reels, and in-store pop-ups, has increased brand awareness by 25%, driving 28% traffic lift and 42% of comp growth, with ROAS outperforming at 4.7x blended.

Now, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Jennifer Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Jennifer Lee (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflationary pressures on your sales?

Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Jennifer. Inflation at 3.2% CPI has led to selective spending, with consumers trading down to our value mid-tier from premiums, but our private labels up 12% basket share and EDLP held ASP +1.8%. Essentials resilient, offsetting discretionary softness, with Sunbelt housing turnover providing tailwinds.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Kim (JPMorgan):
What are your expectations for same-store sales growth in the next quarter?

Mike Patel, Chief Financial Officer:
Good question, David. For Q3, we're guiding comps to 3.5-5.5%, with traffic +2.5-3.5%, supported by remodels, partnerships, and omnichannel holiday lifts. FY24 full year 4-6%, ahead of consensus on Store 2.0 execution.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Torres with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Rachel Torres (Morgan Stanley):
Can you elaborate on the supply chain improvements?

Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Absolutely, Rachel. OTIF at 98.2%, turns 7.2x, freight down 22% via nearshoring 42% to Mexico, AI forecasting errors cut 28%, AMRs boosting throughput 35%. Micro-fulfillment ensures shelf availability, directly adding to comps and margins.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Chris Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Chris Patel (Barclays):
What is the impact from the loyalty program?

Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Great to hear, Chris. Essentials Rewards at 14.2 million members, up 11%, drives 55% of sales, 2x basket, incremental traffic via geo-fenced offers, VIP exclusives adding 50 bps to ticket. Enhancements like beacons will amplify BOPIS and conversion.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Chen with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Laura Chen (Bank of America):
Thanks. On inventory, how sustainable is the turnover improvement?

Mike Patel, Chief Financial Officer:
Laura, 6.2x this quarter, targeting 6.4-6.6x Q3, from AI pricing, VMI 35%, nearshoring, RFID pilots. Store-as-hub omnichannel keeps it fresh, positioning for margin leverage.

Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our long-term strategy. Thank you for your continued support.

Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations:
This concludes today's call. Thank you for joining us.
